problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $25{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}=100.$

activity_context.topic_title: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at the Origin

feedback.problem:
The asymptotes of the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}=8$ are$\,\,y=\pm $
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, we divide both sides of the equation by $8$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2} & =8 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\frac{2{y}^{2}}{8} & =\frac{8}{8} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $a=\sqrt{8}$ and $b=\sqrt{4}=2.$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\pm \frac{2}{\sqrt{8}}x \\  & =\pm \frac{2}{2\sqrt{2}}x \\  & =\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}x \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}x.\end{aligned}
$$
